scenario: 面试官复盘时说：你的 ML 系统设计知识没问题，但这场资深级面试还是没过。
scenario_en: In the debrief the interviewer says your ML system design knowledge is fine, yet you still failed this senior-level round.
q: 为什么资深级 ML 系统设计面试的失败大多不是「不会技术」？
q_en: Why are most senior-level ML system design failures not about lacking technical knowledge?
why: 多数资深失败是行为习惯：钻牛角尖、只铺广度、丢掉业务、不报数字、不讲取舍。像 model drift——权重没变，但输入分布一变表现就退化；你知识没变，一到压力下临场就走样。
why_en: Most senior failures are behavioral habits, not gaps — like model drift where the model is unchanged but performance degrades under a shifted distribution, your knowledge is intact but slips under pressure.
options: 高级岗根本不考技术深度，只看沟通和行为，技术准备是白费
失败几乎都源于某个算法细节没背到，多刷模型和公式就能过关
失败大多是行为习惯——钻牛角尖、只广度、丢业务、不报数字、不讲取舍；知识没变但压力下表现退化，像 model drift
面试结果主要由面试官的主观偏见决定，和候选人当场表现关系不大
options_en: Senior roles don't test technical depth at all, only communication and behavior, so technical prep is wasted.
Failures almost always come from one un-memorized algorithm detail; grinding more models and formulas fixes it.
Most failures are behavioral habits — rabbit-holing, breadth-only, dropping the business, citing no numbers, hiding trade-offs; knowledge is intact but degrades under pressure, like model drift.
The outcome is mostly the interviewer's subjective bias, largely unrelated to the candidate's live performance.
optionExplanations: 太绝对：资深岗照样评技术深度，行为是同等重要的另一半，不是取代技术。
多背模型救不了：真正拖垮人的是临场行为习惯，不是某个算法细节不会。
对；这五种自毁行为反复出现，根因是压力下习惯性走偏，和 model drift 一样——底子在、表现掉。
把责任推给面试官，会让你错过唯一能改的东西：自己可控的临场行为。
optionExplanations_en: Too absolute: senior loops still assess technical depth; behavior is an equally weighted half, not a replacement.
More memorization won't help: what sinks people is live behavioral habits, not a missing algorithm detail.
Correct — these five self-sabotage habits recur; the root cause is drifting off under pressure, just like model drift: fundamentals intact, performance drops.
Blaming the interviewer makes you miss the one thing you control: your own in-room behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型上线后输入数据分布随时间偏移，导致预测表现下降（权重没变、环境变了）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model drift is when a deployed model's performance degrades because the input distribution shifts over time, even though the model itself is unchanged.

termDefinitions.meaning: 几家头部科技大厂的合称，这里泛指高标准的资深级面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAANG refers to the big-tech companies (Meta, Amazon, Apple, Netflix, Google), shorthand here for high-bar senior interviews.

scenario: 你意识到自己刚才跑偏了，想当场把话题拉回来，但不确定按什么顺序说。
scenario_en: You realize you just drifted off-track and want to pull the topic back on the spot, but aren't sure in what order to say it.
q: 把「现场自救脚本」的三拍结构排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the three beats of a live recovery script correctly:
steps: 执行修正后的路线：真的去 zoom out / 报数字 / 讲取舍
承认自己刚才偏了（acknowledge the gap）
说出要怎么纠正（name the correction）
why: 三拍固定：先承认刚才偏了、再说要怎么纠、最后真的执行。不先承认就纠，面试官会觉得你在硬拗；承认了不执行则是空话，所以执行必须收尾。
why_en: The fixed three beats are acknowledge the gap, name the correction, then execute — acknowledging first shows self-awareness, and executing last makes it real instead of just talk.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["1. 承认偏了
acknowledge the gap"] --> B["2. 说出怎么纠
name the correction"] B --> C["3. 真的执行
execute"]

scenario: 你想在面试中及时发现自己有没有踩进五大失败模式，但又不能停下来盯着自己看。
scenario_en: You want to catch yourself falling into the five failure modes during the interview, without freezing to self-monitor.
q: 该以什么节奏做自我检查，才能既抓到走偏又不打断表达？
q_en: At what cadence should you self-monitor to catch drift without breaking your flow?
why: 每 3–4 分钟跑一遍五个诊断问句，正好卡在组件之间的自然过渡点上，所以不打断表达。这不是公式算出来的，而是「一个组件讲完就自检一次」的经验节奏。
why_en: Run the five diagnostic questions every 3-4 minutes, which lands on the natural transition between components so it doesn't break your flow.
options: 每 3–4 分钟、在组件之间的自然过渡点跑一遍五个诊断问句
只在面试官皱眉或打断时才检查，其余时间闷头往下讲
每讲完一句话就自查一次，确保任何时刻都没跑偏
只在面试最后 5 分钟一次性回顾，看有没有漏掉的失败模式
options_en: Every 3-4 minutes, at the natural transition between components, run the five diagnostic questions.
Only check when the interviewer frowns or interrupts, and otherwise push straight ahead.
Self-check after every single sentence so you are never off-track for a moment.
Do one retrospective in the last 5 minutes to see which failure modes you missed.
optionExplanations: 对；3–4 分钟一次刚好对齐组件切换，抓到走偏又不打断节奏，是可持续的自监控频率。
等面试官反应才检查就晚了——失败模式往往在他开口前就已经扣了分。
每句都自查会让你结巴、丢掉连贯表达，反而制造新的负面信号。
留到最后才回顾等于事后诸葛，跑偏的那 10 分钟已经无法挽回。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — every 3-4 minutes aligns with component switches, catching drift without breaking rhythm; it's a sustainable self-monitoring frequency.
Waiting for the interviewer's reaction is too late — the failure mode has usually already cost you before they speak.
Self-checking every sentence makes you stutter and lose coherence, creating a new negative signal.
A retrospective at the end is hindsight; the 10 drifted minutes are already unrecoverable.

termDefinitions.term: 五个诊断问句 / five diagnostic questions
termDefinitions.meaning: 对应五大失败模式的自查问句：我是不是钻牛角尖了？只广不深？丢了业务指标？没报任何数字？没讲取舍？
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The five diagnostic questions map to the five failure modes: am I rabbit-holing, breadth-only, ignoring the business metric, citing no numbers, or hiding trade-offs?

scenario: 复盘手册把资深候选人反复踩的自毁行为归纳成一张五行表，每行配一个诊断信号和自救脚本。
scenario_en: The debrief playbook groups the self-sabotage habits senior candidates repeat into a five-row table, each with a diagnosis signal and a recovery script.
q: 以下哪些是文中总结的「五大自毁行为模式」？(多选)
q_en: Which of these are among the five self-sabotage failure modes? (multiple)
why: 五大模式：钻牛角尖(Rabbit Hole)、只广不深(Shallow Survey)、丢业务(Context Dropout)、不报数字(NFR Blind Spot)、不讲取舍(Silent Trade-off)。「澄清过度」不在其列——反而问需求是被鼓励的行为。
why_en: The five modes are rabbit hole, shallow survey, context dropout, NFR blind spot, and silent trade-off; over-clarifying is not one — asking about requirements is a rewarded behavior.
options: Rabbit Hole 钻牛角尖：卡在一个组件里出不来
Shallow Survey 只广不深：组件全点到但没有任何一个讲透
NFR Blind Spot 不报数字：全程不提延迟/QPS/成本任何量级
Over-Clarifying 澄清过度：一直问需求、迟迟不动手设计
options_en: Rabbit Hole: getting stuck deep inside one component.
Shallow Survey: naming every component but going deep on none.
NFR Blind Spot: citing no numbers at all (latency / QPS / cost).
Over-Clarifying: endlessly asking about requirements and never starting the design.
optionExplanations: 对；钻牛角尖是第一大模式——压力把专长激活，你误把深度当成严谨。
对；只广不深读起来像背课本，缺少动手过的痕迹（内部机制与取舍）。
对；一个数字都不报会显得你只懂学术精度、不懂生产约束。
错；这不是五大模式之一。适度澄清需求恰恰是被奖励的资深行为，只有多到面试官要打断你才算问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the rabbit hole is the first mode: pressure activates your expertise and you mistake depth for rigor.
Correct — a shallow survey reads like textbook recitation, missing the fingerprints of hands-on work (internals and trade-offs).
Correct — citing zero numbers signals you only know academic accuracy, not production constraints.
Incorrect — this is not one of the five. Sensible requirement clarification is a rewarded senior behavior; only asking so much that the interviewer must redirect you is a problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统必须满足的运行约束，如延迟、吞吐(QPS)、成本、可解释性，而非「系统做什么」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An NFR (Non-Functional Requirement) is an operating constraint the system must meet — latency, throughput (QPS), cost, explainability — rather than what the system does.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求/预测数，衡量吞吐量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) measures throughput as requests or predictions handled each second.

scenario: 你已经花 8 分钟调 HNSW 索引的 ef_construction 和距离度量，而 ranking、serving、业务指标一个都还没提。
scenario_en: You've spent 8 minutes tuning the HNSW index's ef_construction and distance metric, while ranking, serving, and the business metric are still untouched.
q: 此刻最该做的一步是什么？
q_en: What's the single best move right now?
why: 钻牛角尖的信号是 >3 分钟卡在一个组件、不回连整条 pipeline。自救三拍：承认刚才太深→说要 zoom out→真的画出端到端流程再一起选深挖点。面试官持续奖励这种自我纠偏。
why_en: The rabbit-hole signal is over three minutes on one component without linking back to the pipeline; the fix is to acknowledge, zoom out, and jointly pick where to go deep.
whenOtherWins: 如果是面试官明确点名要你深入这个索引组件，那继续深挖才是对的——此时不该 zoom out。
options: 继续深挖索引参数，把这块讲到极致，用深度证明专业度
主动 zoom out，先画出端到端流程，再和面试官一起决定哪个组件值得深挖
默默跳到另一个组件，不解释为什么换，继续往下讲
承认跑偏后就停住，把「深挖哪一块」的决定完全甩给面试官
options_en: Keep drilling the index parameters and cover them exhaustively, using depth to prove expertise.
Zoom out on your own initiative, sketch the end-to-end flow, then jointly decide with the interviewer which component deserves the deep dive.
Silently jump to another component without explaining the switch and carry on.
Acknowledge the drift, then stop and hand the 'which part to go deep on' decision entirely to the interviewer.
optionExplanations: 越深挖越坐实钻牛角尖：8 分钟不回连 pipeline，读作你不会管理范围。
对；主动 zoom out 展示端到端判断力，再共同选深挖点，把失控扳回受控。
无声跳走没有承认这一拍，面试官只看到你飘忽不定，仍不知你有没有全局观。
承认之后要自己给出修正路线；把决定全甩给面试官等于放弃主导权。
optionExplanations_en: Drilling deeper cements the rabbit hole: 8 minutes without linking back reads as an inability to manage scope.
Correct — zooming out shows end-to-end judgment, and jointly picking the deep dive turns loss of control back into control.
Silently jumping skips the acknowledge beat; the interviewer just sees you wander and still can't tell if you have a global view.
After acknowledging you must offer the correction yourself; handing the whole decision over abandons your leadership of the session.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种近似最近邻(ANN)图索引，用于向量检索的快速召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is an approximate-nearest-neighbor graph index used for fast vector retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: HNSW 建图时的搜索宽度参数：越大图质量越高、构建越慢，属于很细的调参项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ef_construction is HNSW's build-time search width: larger gives a higher-quality graph but slower construction — a very fine-grained tuning knob.

scenario: 压力上来时，你本能地往一个熟悉的组件里越钻越深，感觉「我在很严谨地设计」。
scenario_en: Under pressure you instinctively drill deeper into a familiar component, and it feels like 'I'm designing rigorously.'
q: 为什么这种「感觉很扎实」的深挖反而是高危信号？
q_en: Why is this 'feels solid' deep dive actually a high-risk signal?
why: 压力会激活你的专长，让你把深度误当成严谨——但对面看到的是你 3 分钟不回连 pipeline、没有端到端判断力。自我纠偏（zoom out）才是持续被奖励的行为。
why_en: Pressure activates your expertise and you mistake depth for rigor, but the interviewer sees three minutes without linking back and no end-to-end judgment; self-correction is what's consistently rewarded.
options: 深挖一定是好事，越细越能拿高分，感觉扎实就说明方向对
危险在于压力把专长激活、让你误把深度当严谨，却丢掉了端到端判断力这个真正被考的信号
危险在于深挖会用光时间，但只要最后赶紧把别的组件也点一遍就没事
这其实不是问题，面试官更喜欢一头扎进单点、把一个组件讲到底的候选人
options_en: Deep diving is always good — the finer the higher the score, and feeling solid means the direction is right.
The danger is that pressure activates your expertise and you mistake depth for rigor, while losing the end-to-end judgment that is actually being assessed.
The danger is only that deep diving burns time, but as long as you quickly name the other components at the end it's fine.
It isn't really a problem — interviewers prefer candidates who dive into one point and exhaust a single component.
optionExplanations: 「感觉扎实」正是陷阱：它像自信和推进感，却掩盖了你没在展示全局判断。
对；根因是压力触发专长，把深度当严谨；被考的其实是你能否管理范围、回连业务。
补一遍别的组件治标不治本，会滑向另一个失败模式（只广不深）。
说反了：一头扎到底、不回连 pipeline，正是资深面试里最常见的扣分点。
optionExplanations_en: 'Feels solid' is exactly the trap: it mimics confidence and momentum while hiding that you're not showing global judgment.
Correct — the root cause is pressure triggering expertise, mistaking depth for rigor; what's tested is whether you manage scope and reconnect to the business.
Tacking the other components on at the end treats the symptom and slides you into the other failure mode (shallow survey).
Backwards: diving to the bottom without reconnecting to the pipeline is one of the most common deductions in senior interviews.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从特征、召回、排序到 serving、反馈的完整链路；钻牛角尖就是长时间不回连这条链。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The pipeline is the full chain from features, retrieval, ranking to serving and feedback; rabbit-holing is going too long without reconnecting to it.

scenario: 你一口气点了 feature store、embedding、检索、排序、重排、serving、日志、A/B 八个组件，每个只讲了一两句。
scenario_en: You've named eight components in a row — feature store, embeddings, retrieval, ranking, re-ranking, serving, logging, A/B — one or two sentences each.
q: 此刻最该做的一步是什么？
q_en: What's the single best move right now?
why: 只广不深的信号是点了 >5 个组件却没讲透任何一个，读作背课本。自救：承认已铺完高层架构→挑「取舍最有意思」的那个组件→真的走进去讲内部机制和权衡。
why_en: The shallow-survey signal is naming over five components without going deep on any; the fix is to acknowledge the architecture is outlined, pick the component with the most interesting trade-offs, and actually walk through it.
whenOtherWins: 在开场刚要建立高层蓝图、面试官也想先看全景时，先快速铺一遍所有组件是对的——广度阶段本就该点名。
options: 再补充几个之前没提到的组件，把架构图铺得更全面
承认已铺完高层架构，挑出取舍最有意思的一个组件，走进去讲内部机制和权衡
从头把八个组件按顺序再讲一遍，这次每个多说几句
直接问面试官想听哪个，自己不做取舍判断
options_en: Add a few more components you haven't mentioned to make the architecture diagram even more complete.
Acknowledge the high-level architecture is outlined, pick the one component with the most interesting trade-offs, and walk through its internals and trade-offs.
Go through all eight components again in order, this time saying a few more sentences on each.
Just ask the interviewer which one they want to hear, without making the trade-off judgment yourself.
optionExplanations: 再加组件只会加深「只广不深」，把背课本的印象坐得更实。
对；主动收敛到一个高取舍组件深挖，用一次真正的深入证明你动过手、有判断力。
重讲一遍还是浅——多说几句不等于讲透内部机制和权衡。
全甩给面试官等于放弃「挑最有价值组件」这个恰恰在被考的判断。
optionExplanations_en: Adding components deepens the shallow survey and cements the textbook-recitation impression.
Correct — converging on one high-trade-off component and going deep proves with a single real dive that you've done the work and have judgment.
Re-listing is still shallow — a few more sentences each is not the same as exhausting internals and trade-offs.
Handing it entirely to the interviewer abandons the very judgment being tested: picking the most valuable component.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一存储和服务模型特征的系统，保证训练与线上取到一致特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store centrally stores and serves model features so training and serving read consistent values.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在初排结果上再用更重的模型/规则做二次排序，通常只作用于少量候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-ranking applies a heavier model or rules to reorder an already-ranked shortlist, usually over few candidates.

scenario: 从只广不深里自救时，你要挑「取舍最有意思」的组件深挖，题目是一个对延迟极敏感的广告排序系统。
scenario_en: Recovering from a shallow survey, you must pick the component with the most interesting trade-offs to go deep on; the problem is a latency-sensitive ads-ranking system.
q: 在延迟敏感的广告排序里，应该深挖哪个组件？
q_en: In latency-sensitive ads ranking, which component should you go deep on?
why: 「最有意思」= 被业务问题约束最紧的那个组件。延迟敏感的广告排序里，serving/ranking 层承受 50ms 级 SLA 的压力，取舍最密集；离线特征管线不在这条关键路径上。
why_en: 'Most interesting' means the component most constrained by the business problem; for latency-sensitive ads ranking that's the serving/ranking layer under a tight SLA, not the offline feature pipeline.
whenOtherWins: 如果瓶颈其实在数据侧（如特征新鲜度决定成败、召回质量差），那离线特征管线才是该深挖的高取舍组件。
options: 离线特征管线，因为它数据量最大、工程最复杂
日志与监控，因为它和最终指标直接相关
serving/ranking 层，因为它被延迟 SLA 约束最紧、取舍最密集，正是业务问题的痛点所在
A/B 实验框架，因为所有决策最后都要靠它验证
options_en: The offline feature pipeline, because it has the most data and the most engineering complexity.
Logging and monitoring, because it's directly tied to the final metrics.
The serving/ranking layer, because it's most tightly bound by the latency SLA and packed with trade-offs — exactly where the business problem bites.
The A/B testing framework, because every decision ultimately gets validated there.
optionExplanations: 离线管线不在延迟关键路径上，工程再复杂也不是这道题的痛点。
日志重要但不是延迟敏感排序的核心取舍点，深挖它显示不出你抓主要矛盾。
对；把深挖对准业务约束最紧的层，才是从只广不深里救回来的正确落点。
A/B 是验证手段，不是这道延迟题里取舍最密集、最该深挖的组件。
optionExplanations_en: The offline pipeline isn't on the latency-critical path; however complex, it's not this problem's pain point.
Logging matters but isn't the core trade-off of latency-sensitive ranking; diving there doesn't show you grasp the main tension.
Correct — pointing the deep dive at the layer most constrained by the business is the right landing spot when recovering from a shallow survey.
A/B is a validation mechanism, not the most trade-off-dense component to deep-dive in this latency-bound problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对外承诺的服务指标（如响应延迟上限），未达标有后果；这里指广告拍卖的延迟上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed service target such as a maximum response latency, here the ad auction's latency ceiling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上实时给请求打分、返回结果的推理服务，直接承受延迟约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The serving layer is the online inference service that scores requests and returns results in real time, directly bearing the latency constraint.

scenario: 你已经连着讲了 5 分钟一个很优雅的欺诈检测 GNN 架构，全程在优化 AUC，但没提过任何业务指标或用户影响。
scenario_en: You've spent 5 minutes on an elegant fraud-detection GNN architecture, all about optimizing AUC, with no mention of any business metric or user impact.
q: 此刻最该做的一步是什么？
q_en: What's the single best move right now?
why: 丢业务的信号是最近 5 分钟没提任何业务指标或用户影响。自救：把设计显式接回业务目标——「我选它是因为它优化了[业务指标]，而这重要是因为[原因]」。在 Staff+，业务对齐和技术深度同等加权。
why_en: The context-dropout signal is five minutes with no business metric or user impact; the fix is to explicitly reconnect the design to the business goal, since at Staff+ business alignment is weighted as heavily as technical depth.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官刚明确要求你只讲纯技术实现细节（如模型结构），那暂时聚焦技术、稍后再接回业务是合理的。
options: 继续把 GNN 的消息传递和采样策略讲得更深，技术足够强业务自然不重要
把设计显式接回业务目标：我选它是因为它优化了漏报带来的资金损失，这对支付方最关键
换个话题聊聊模型部署和监控，绕开业务不谈
反问面试官这道题的业务目标到底是什么，把定义责任推回去
options_en: Keep going deeper on the GNN's message passing and sampling, since strong enough tech makes the business irrelevant.
Explicitly reconnect the design to the business goal: I chose it because it minimizes the money lost to false negatives, which matters most to the payment provider.
Switch topics to deployment and monitoring, steering around the business entirely.
Ask the interviewer what the business objective even is, pushing the definition back onto them.
optionExplanations: 技术再强也救不了丢业务：Staff+ 把业务对齐和技术深度同等加权，只讲技术等于丢一半分。
对；一句「优化了什么业务指标、为什么重要」就把技术接回价值，正是自救的执行拍。
换话题是继续回避业务，信号不会消失，只会拖到结尾坐实。
开场就该澄清业务；讲了 5 分钟才反问，暴露你一直没带着业务目标设计。
optionExplanations_en: No amount of tech saves a context dropout: Staff+ weights business alignment as heavily as depth, so tech-only loses half the score.
Correct — one line naming the business metric optimized and why it matters reconnects tech to value; that's the execute beat of the recovery.
Switching topics keeps dodging the business; the signal doesn't vanish, it just cements by the end.
The business should be clarified up front; asking after 5 minutes reveals you were never designing toward a business goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在图结构上做消息传递学习节点/边表示的模型，常用于欺诈检测里的关系建模。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GNN (Graph Neural Network) learns node/edge representations by passing messages over a graph, common for relational modeling in fraud detection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分类器排序能力的离线指标，衡量把正样本排在负样本前的概率；它是技术指标，不等于业务价值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is an offline ranking metric — the probability a positive is scored above a negative — a technical metric, not business value.

termDefinitions.meaning: Staff 及以上工程师级别，面试要求业务对齐与技术深度并重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Staff+ denotes staff-level and above engineers, where interviews weight business alignment alongside technical depth.

scenario: 一个技术上很漂亮的欺诈 GNN，全程只优化 AUC，从没讨论漏报(FN)和误报(FP)各自的美元代价。
scenario_en: A technically beautiful fraud GNN optimizes AUC throughout and never discusses the dollar cost of false negatives versus false positives.
q: 在 Staff+ 评估里，这样一个「优雅但不谈业务」的设计会怎样？
q_en: In a Staff+ assessment, how does this 'elegant but business-blind' design fare?
why: 漏报和误报的美元代价通常极不对称——放过一笔欺诈亏的钱，和误拦一个好用户造成的流失，代价差很多，这决定阈值和损失函数。只优化 AUC 而不谈这笔账，在 Staff+ 会因业务对齐缺失而扣掉一半分。
why_en: The dollar costs of false negatives and false positives are usually very asymmetric, which should set the threshold and loss; optimizing AUC alone ignores that ledger and loses heavily on business alignment at Staff+.
options: 会拿高分，因为 AUC 高就代表模型好，业务细节可以留给产品团队
无所谓，反正 Staff+ 只看架构是否新颖优雅
会明显扣分：FN 与 FP 的美元代价高度不对称、本应决定阈值与损失函数，只谈 AUC 暴露业务对齐缺失
只会小扣一点，业务对齐在 Staff+ 权重很低
options_en: It scores high, because a high AUC means a good model and business details can be left to the product team.
It doesn't matter, since Staff+ only cares whether the architecture is novel and elegant.
It's clearly penalized: FN and FP dollar costs are highly asymmetric and should set the threshold and loss, so AUC-only exposes missing business alignment.
It's only lightly penalized, since business alignment carries little weight at Staff+.
optionExplanations: AUC 高不等于赚钱：不谈 FN/FP 代价，模型可能优化了一个和收益错位的目标。
说反了：Staff+ 恰恰把业务对齐抬到和技术深度同等的高度。
对；把漏报/误报换算成钱，才能定阈值和损失函数——这正是资深候选人该主动交代的账。
低估了权重：在 Staff+，业务对齐和技术深度同等加权，缺它会实打实扣一大块。
optionExplanations_en: High AUC doesn't mean profit: without FN/FP costs the model may be optimizing an objective misaligned with revenue.
Backwards: Staff+ specifically raises business alignment to the same level as technical depth.
Correct — converting false negatives/positives into money is what sets the threshold and loss, exactly the ledger a senior candidate should volunteer.
It underestimates the weight: at Staff+ business alignment is weighted equally with depth, and missing it costs real points.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把真欺诈判成正常，放过一笔欺诈，直接造成资金损失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative (FN) labels real fraud as normal, letting fraud through and causing direct money loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把正常交易判成欺诈，误拦好用户，造成体验损失与流失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive (FP) labels a legitimate transaction as fraud, blocking a good user and causing friction and churn.

scenario: 你为搜索页设计了一个把相关性提升 +3% 的重排模型，但整场没报过任何延迟数字，而搜索页 p99 延迟 SLO 大约是 200ms。
scenario_en: You designed a re-ranker that lifts search relevance by +3%, but cited no latency numbers all session, while the search page's p99 latency SLO is around 200ms.
q: 这个「不报数字」的习惯为什么可能让整个设计作废？
q_en: Why can this 'no numbers' habit invalidate the whole design?
why: NFR 是首要设计驱动：一个 +3% 相关性的重排，如果把 p99 顶过 200ms SLO，用户根本等不到它、等于白做。面试不要求精确 SLO，给合理量级即可——如「搜索 <200ms p99」「广告 serving ~50K QPS」。
why_en: NFRs are primary design drivers: a +3% re-ranker that pushes p99 past the 200ms SLO is useless because users never wait for it; rough estimates like search <200ms p99 or ad serving ~50K QPS are enough.
options: 不会有问题，相关性 +3% 是硬收益，延迟慢一点用户会愿意等
因为面试必须报出精确到毫秒的官方 SLO，报不出就算失败
因为 NFR 是首要约束：+3% 相关性若把 p99 顶过 200ms SLO 就等于不可用，报个合理量级(如搜索 <200ms)即可
因为数字只在给出精确成本预算时才有意义，延迟不影响模型是否可用
options_en: No problem — +3% relevance is a hard gain, and users will happily wait a bit longer for it.
Because interviews require citing the exact official SLO down to the millisecond, and failing to means failure.
Because NFRs are the primary constraint: a +3% re-ranker that pushes p99 past the 200ms SLO is effectively unusable; a rough magnitude like search <200ms suffices.
Because numbers only matter when giving an exact cost budget; latency doesn't affect whether the model is usable.
optionExplanations: 用户不会等：搜索页超时的模型分数来得太晚，+3% 相关性也救不了不可用。
过头了：不需要精确官方 SLO，合理量级估计就够——重点是有没有用数字约束设计。
对；先把延迟/QPS 量级钉下来，才能判断这个重排到底能不能上线，这正是 NFR 作为首要驱动的意义。
延迟本身就决定可用性：一个 200ms SLO 的搜索页装不下拖慢它的重排。
optionExplanations_en: Users won't wait: a model whose score arrives after the search page times out can't be saved by +3% relevance.
Overshoot: you don't need the exact official SLO; a reasonable magnitude is enough — the point is whether you constrain the design with numbers.
Correct — pinning latency/QPS magnitudes first tells you whether the re-ranker is even deployable, which is what makes NFRs a primary driver.
Latency itself decides usability: a search page with a 200ms SLO can't absorb a re-ranker that slows it down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的请求都比这个延迟快；比均值更能反映最慢那批用户的体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the value 99% of requests come in under, reflecting the slow tail of user experience better than the mean.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内部设定的服务目标（如 p99<200ms），是给定目标而非公式推导结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is an internal service target like p99 under 200ms — a given goal, not a value derived from a formula.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在初排后用更重的模型对少量候选再排序，提升相关性但增加延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A re-ranker reorders a small candidate shortlist with a heavier model, lifting relevance at the cost of latency.

scenario: 被问召回架构时你直接说「我会用 two-tower 双塔模型」，没说它换来什么、牺牲了什么。
scenario_en: Asked about the retrieval architecture, you flatly say 'I'd use a two-tower model,' without stating what it gains or gives up.
q: 此刻最该补上的一句是什么？
q_en: What's the one line you most need to add right now?
why: 沉默取舍的信号是「我会用 X」却不说得失，在资深级读作在瞎猜。自救：一句话点名取舍轴——双塔换来 serving 高效（物品向量可预计算），代价是丢掉 cross-encoder 那种细粒度 query-item 交互。
why_en: The silent-trade-off signal is 'I'd use X' with no gain/loss, which reads as guessing at senior level; the fix is one line naming the axis — two-tower buys serving efficiency but gives up fine-grained query-item interaction.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官已经和你一起确认过这个取舍、只想快速推进到下一步，就不必每次都重复展开得失。
options: 补一句更自信的话：双塔是业界标准做法，选它准没错
补一句取舍：双塔换来 serving 高效（物品向量可预计算），代价是丢掉 cross-encoder 的细粒度 query-item 交互
补充双塔的训练细节，比如用了哪种负采样
改口说其实哪个模型都行，避免被追问得失
options_en: Add a more confident line: two-tower is the industry standard, so picking it can't be wrong.
Add the trade-off: two-tower buys serving efficiency (item vectors are precomputable) at the cost of the fine-grained query-item interaction a cross-encoder captures.
Add training details of the two-tower, like which negative sampling you used.
Backpedal and say any model would do, to avoid being pressed on gains and losses.
optionExplanations: 「业界标准」不是取舍，反而更像在背模板；资深级要的是你能说出得与失。
对；一句「gives us…costs us…」点名取舍轴，把瞎猜变成有依据的决策。
训练细节是另一层深度，回答不了「你为什么选它、放弃了什么」这个取舍问题。
改口说都行是最差的：既没取舍又显得没主见，直接坐实沉默取舍。
optionExplanations_en: 'Industry standard' isn't a trade-off and sounds like reciting a template; senior level wants the gain and the loss.
Correct — one 'gives us... costs us...' line names the trade-off axis and turns a guess into a grounded decision.
Training details are a different depth and don't answer why you chose it and what you gave up.
Backpedaling to 'any works' is worst: no trade-off and no conviction, cementing the silent trade-off.

termDefinitions.meaning: query 和 item 各用一个塔编码成向量，靠向量内积匹配；物品向量可离线预计算，serving 快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model encodes query and item with separate towers into vectors matched by dot product; item vectors can be precomputed offline for fast serving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 query 和 item 拼在一起同时编码，能捕捉细粒度交互但无法预计算、serving 贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder jointly encodes query and item together, capturing fine-grained interaction but can't be precomputed, making serving expensive.

scenario: 双塔(two-tower)和 cross-encoder 都能给 query 和 item 打匹配分，你要一句话说清为什么召回阶段常选双塔。
scenario_en: Both two-tower and cross-encoder score query-item match; you must state in one line why retrieval usually picks two-tower.
q: 召回阶段选双塔而非 cross-encoder，换来什么、牺牲什么？
q_en: Choosing two-tower over a cross-encoder for retrieval — what's gained and what's lost?
why: 双塔换来 serving 高效：物品向量可离线预计算、线上只算一次 query 向量再做近邻检索，能在毫秒级从千万级物品里召回。代价是塔各自独立编码，丢掉了 cross-encoder 那种把 query 和 item 拼在一起才能捕捉的细粒度交互。
why_en: Two-tower buys serving efficiency — item vectors are precomputed so only the query is encoded online — at the cost of the fine-grained query-item interaction a cross-encoder captures by joint encoding.
tradeoff: 双塔(可预计算、serving 快) vs cross-encoder(细粒度交互强、但每对都要现算、serving 贵)
options: 双塔更快但更不准，cross-encoder 又快又准，只是工程复杂所以少用
双塔换来 serving 高效（物品向量可预计算），牺牲了 cross-encoder 的细粒度 query-item 交互精度
两者完全等价，只是命名不同，选哪个不影响延迟和精度
cross-encoder 可预计算所以 serving 更快，双塔必须每对现算所以慢
options_en: Two-tower is faster but less accurate; cross-encoder is both fast and accurate and only rarely used because it's complex.
Two-tower buys serving efficiency (item vectors precomputable) at the cost of the fine-grained query-item interaction accuracy of a cross-encoder.
They're fully equivalent, just named differently, and the choice affects neither latency nor accuracy.
The cross-encoder is precomputable so it serves faster, while two-tower must score each pair live and is slower.
optionExplanations: cross-encoder 并非又快又准：它精度高但每个 query-item 对都要现算，在千万级候选上 serving 扛不住。
对；双塔的可预计算换来毫秒级大规模召回，代价是牺牲了拼接编码才有的细粒度交互。
并不等价：可预计算与否直接决定能否在延迟内从海量物品召回，精度侧也有差。
说反了：可预计算的是双塔（物品向量离线算好），cross-encoder 才是每对现算的那个。
optionExplanations_en: A cross-encoder isn't both fast and accurate: it's accurate but must score every query-item pair live, which can't scale to tens of millions of candidates.
Correct — two-tower's precomputability buys millisecond large-scale retrieval, at the cost of the fine-grained interaction only joint encoding gives.
Not equivalent: precomputability decides whether you can retrieve from a huge corpus within latency, and accuracy differs too.
Backwards: two-tower is the precomputable one (item vectors computed offline); the cross-encoder scores each pair live.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  subgraph TwoTower["双塔 two-tower"]
    Q1["query 塔"] --> V1["query 向量"]
    I1["item 塔(离线预计算)"] --> V2["item 向量库"]
    V1 --> M1["内积/ANN 匹配"]
    V2 --> M1
  end
  subgraph Cross["cross-encoder"]
    QI["query+item 拼接"] --> ENC["联合编码"] --> S["匹配分(每对现算)"]
  end

termDefinitions.meaning: 在向量空间里快速找最接近 query 向量的物品，用近似换速度，支撑双塔的大规模召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search quickly finds items closest to the query vector, trading exactness for speed to power large-scale two-tower retrieval.

scenario: 你在准备资深级面试，想知道哪一个习惯性动作对评分的正向影响最大。
scenario_en: Preparing for senior interviews, you want to know which single habit most positively affects your score.
q: 在 senior/Staff+ 面试里，单个最高信号的行为是什么？
q_en: What is the single highest-signal behavior in senior/Staff+ interviews?
why: 显式的取舍推理是 senior/Staff+ 单个最高信号的行为。光说「我会用 X」在资深级读作瞎猜；把每个决策说成「换来什么、牺牲什么、为什么在本情境下我选它」，才证明你在做工程判断而非套模板。
why_en: Explicit trade-off reasoning is the single highest-signal behavior at senior/Staff+; a bare 'I'd use X' reads as guessing, while naming gain, loss, and why-here proves engineering judgment.
options: 把尽可能多的组件都点到，展示知识面广
显式的取舍推理：每个决策都说清换来什么、牺牲什么、为什么本情境选它
在一个熟悉的组件上钻得越深越好，证明技术硬
尽量用最新的模型架构名词，显得紧跟前沿
options_en: Name as many components as possible to show breadth of knowledge.
Explicit trade-off reasoning: for each decision state what's gained, what's lost, and why it fits here.
Drill as deep as possible into one familiar component to prove technical strength.
Drop the newest model-architecture terms to seem on the cutting edge.
optionExplanations: 点满组件正是「只广不深」失败模式，广度本身不是高信号。
对；取舍推理直接展示工程判断，是资深级评分权重最高的单个动作。
钻太深是「钻牛角尖」失败模式，深度不回连全局并不加分。
堆名词不等于判断力，反而容易在被追问得失时露馅。
optionExplanations_en: Maxing out components is the shallow-survey failure mode; breadth alone isn't high signal.
Correct — trade-off reasoning directly displays engineering judgment, the single most heavily weighted behavior at senior level.
Drilling too deep is the rabbit-hole failure mode; depth that never reconnects to the whole doesn't score.
Piling on terms isn't judgment and tends to collapse when you're pressed on gains and losses.

scenario: 为了即使紧张也能强制自己讲取舍，文中给了一个句法习惯。
scenario_en: To force yourself to state trade-offs even when nervous, the lesson gives a syntactic habit.
q: 把每个设计决策都说成含哪两个短语的句子，就能逼出取舍表达？
q_en: Framing every design decision as a sentence containing which two phrases forces trade-off articulation?
text: 把每个设计决策说成一句同时含「{{gives us}}」（换来什么）和「{{costs us}}」（牺牲什么）的话——这个句法习惯即使在紧张时也能逼你把取舍讲出来。
text_en: Frame every design decision as a sentence containing both '{{gives us}}' and '{{costs us}}' — this syntactic habit forces trade-off articulation even when you're nervous.
why: 「gives us / costs us」是一个可随身携带的句法钩子：句子结构本身要求你填上得与失，于是紧张时也不会漏讲取舍，直接对治沉默取舍这个失败模式。
why_en: 'Gives us / costs us' is a portable syntactic hook whose very structure demands you fill in the gain and the loss, so trade-offs survive even nerves.

scenario: 复盘手册说，失败模式自救脚本和之前学的「4 步 pushback 框架」是互补的两套工具。
scenario_en: The playbook says the failure-mode recovery scripts and the earlier '4-step pushback framework' are two complementary tools.
q: pushback 恢复和失败模式恢复，触发来源有什么区别？
q_en: How do pushback recovery and failure-mode recovery differ in what triggers them?
why: pushback 恢复应对面试官发起的约束变更（他改了规模/延迟/需求），是被动接招；失败模式恢复是你自己发起的临场纠偏（发现钻牛角尖就 zoom out），是主动自救。两者合起来才是完整的抗压工具箱。
why_en: Pushback recovery answers interviewer-initiated constraint changes, while failure-mode recovery is self-initiated course correction; together they form the full resilience toolkit.
tradeoff: pushback 恢复(面试官发起、被动接招) vs 失败模式恢复(自己发起、主动纠偏)
options: 两者都是面试官发起的，只是一个改约束、一个改题目
pushback 恢复是面试官发起的约束变更；失败模式恢复是你自己发起的临场纠偏，二者互补
两者都是候选人自己发起的，只是话术不同
pushback 恢复只在编码轮用，失败模式恢复只在系统设计轮用
options_en: Both are interviewer-initiated; one changes constraints and the other changes the problem.
Pushback recovery handles interviewer-initiated constraint changes; failure-mode recovery is self-initiated course correction — the two are complementary.
Both are candidate-initiated and differ only in wording.
Pushback recovery is only for coding rounds and failure-mode recovery only for system design rounds.
optionExplanations: 混淆了触发源：失败模式恢复不是面试官发起的，是你自己察觉走偏后主动做的。
对；一个应对外部约束变更、一个应对自己走偏，触发源正好相反，合起来覆盖两类风险。
说反了一半：pushback 是面试官发起的，不是候选人自己发起。
两套工具跨轮次通用，不限定编码或系统设计。
optionExplanations_en: Confuses the trigger: failure-mode recovery isn't interviewer-initiated; you do it after noticing your own drift.
Correct — one answers external constraint changes and one answers your own drift; opposite triggers that together cover both risk types.
Half-backwards: pushback is interviewer-initiated, not candidate-initiated.
Both tools apply across rounds and aren't limited to coding or system design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应对面试官临场改约束（改规模/延迟/需求）的 4 步应对法，属被面试官发起的恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The pushback framework is a 4-step method for handling interviewer-initiated constraint changes (scale/latency/requirement shifts).

scenario: 官方给的自救话术念起来不像你平时说话，你想改成自己的口吻。
scenario_en: The official recovery scripts don't sound like how you normally talk, and you want to adapt them to your own voice.
q: 个性化自救话术时，哪一点绝不能动？
q_en: When personalizing a recovery script, what must you never change?
why: 措辞可以改成你自己的口吻、更自然，但必须保住三拍结构：承认偏了→说出怎么纠→真的执行。丢掉承认这一拍会显得遮掩，丢掉执行会变空话，结构才是话术起作用的骨架。
why_en: Adapt the wording to your own voice, but preserve the three-beat structure — acknowledge, name the correction, execute — because the structure, not the phrasing, is what makes the script work.
whenOtherWins: 如果某个场景天然只需要一步（比如只是补一个数字），可以压缩表达，但仍要保留「承认+执行」的最小闭环。
options: 必须一字不差背原话，任何改写都会削弱效果
措辞可自由改成自己的口吻，但要保住「承认→纠正→执行」三拍结构
只要保留执行这一拍就行，承认和说纠正都可以省
把话术改得越长越正式越好，显得准备充分
options_en: Recite the exact wording verbatim, since any rewrite weakens it.
Freely adapt the wording to your own voice, but preserve the three-beat structure (acknowledge, correct, execute).
Keep only the execute beat; acknowledging and naming the correction can be dropped.
Make the script as long and formal as possible to seem well-prepared.
optionExplanations: 背原话反而僵硬、像念稿；自然口吻更可信，可改的正是措辞。
对；骨架（三拍）保住、血肉（措辞）随你，这样既自然又不丢自救的有效结构。
省掉承认会显得遮掩、省掉说纠正会突兀，三拍缺一恢复就不完整。
越长越正式反而显得在背模板，简短自然的三拍才有效。
optionExplanations_en: Verbatim recital sounds stiff and scripted; a natural voice is more credible, and wording is exactly what you may change.
Correct — keep the skeleton (three beats), let the flesh (wording) be yours, staying natural without losing the effective structure.
Dropping acknowledge looks evasive and dropping name-the-correction feels abrupt; missing any beat leaves the recovery incomplete.
Longer and more formal reads as reciting a template; a short, natural three-beat is what works.

scenario: 五大失败模式各有一个可当场自查的诊断阈值，用来判断自己是不是踩进去了。
scenario_en: Each of the five failure modes has a self-checkable diagnostic threshold to tell whether you've fallen in.
q: 补全钻牛角尖和只广不深的两个诊断阈值：
q_en: Fill in the two diagnostic thresholds for rabbit hole and shallow survey:
text: 钻牛角尖(Rabbit Hole)的信号：在一个组件上停留超过 {{3}} 分钟却没回连 pipeline；只广不深(Shallow Survey)的信号：点了超过 {{5}} 个组件却没讲透任何一个的内部机制与取舍。
text_en: Rabbit-hole signal: over {{3}} minutes on one component without linking back to the pipeline; shallow-survey signal: naming more than {{5}} components without going deep on any one's internals and trade-offs.
why: 这两个是可当场数的阈值：单组件 >3 分钟、或点名 >5 个组件都没讲透，就该触发自救。它们不是硬定律，而是让你在压力下快速自查的经验红线。
why_en: These are countable in-room thresholds — over three minutes on one component, or more than five named without depth — that trigger recovery; they're rules of thumb, not hard laws.

scenario: 你想理解为什么学术背景强的候选人特别容易犯「不报数字(NFR Blind Spot)」这个失败模式。
scenario_en: You want to understand why academically strong candidates are especially prone to the NFR-blind-spot failure mode.
q: 「不报数字」这个失败模式的根因通常是什么？
q_en: What's the usual root cause of the NFR-blind-spot failure mode?
why: 根因是学术训练把重心放在模型精度上、很少练运维约束，所以答题时本能盯着 accuracy/AUC，忘了延迟、QPS、成本这些生产里真正决定可行性的量级。对治办法是开场就主动锚定 NFR。
why_en: The root cause is that academic training emphasizes accuracy over operational constraints, so candidates fixate on accuracy/AUC and forget the latency, QPS, and cost magnitudes that decide feasibility in production.
options: 候选人故意不报数字，想藏住自己不会估算
学术训练强调模型精度、少练运维约束，所以本能忽略延迟/QPS/成本这些生产量级
因为面试题从不提供任何数字，报了也没依据
因为报数字属于高级技巧，初级候选人还没资格用
options_en: Candidates deliberately cite no numbers to hide that they can't estimate.
Academic training emphasizes model accuracy over operational constraints, so latency/QPS/cost magnitudes get instinctively ignored.
Because interview prompts never provide any numbers, so any figure would be unfounded.
Because citing numbers is an advanced skill juniors aren't yet qualified to use.
optionExplanations: 多数不是故意藏拙，而是训练重心让人根本没想到要报运维数字。
对；学术偏精度、轻运维的惯性，让人盯着 AUC 忘了延迟/QPS/成本这些首要约束。
题目常故意不给 NFR，正是要考你主动补——不给数字不等于没约束。
报数字不是资历门槛，恰恰是资深级被期待的基本动作。
optionExplanations_en: It's usually not deliberate hiding but a training bias that never prompts operational numbers.
Correct — the accuracy-over-ops habit from academia makes people watch AUC and forget latency/QPS/cost, the primary constraints.
Prompts often omit NFRs on purpose to test if you surface them — no numbers given doesn't mean no constraints.
Citing numbers isn't a seniority gate; it's precisely the baseline move expected at senior level.

scenario: 你想在模拟面试里系统性地练掉这五个失败模式，而不只是靠自己感觉。
scenario_en: You want to systematically train away the five failure modes in mock interviews, not just by feel.
q: 文中推荐的「搭档辅助练习」具体怎么做？
q_en: What is the recommended partner-assisted practice method?
why: 让模拟搭档在你答题时安静地记录出现了哪些失败模式，结束后对着那张五模式表逐条复盘。第三方视角能抓到你自己察觉不到的走偏，比闷头自练更快看到盲区。
why_en: Have a mock partner silently track which failure modes appear while you answer, then debrief against the five-mode table; an outside view catches drift you can't see yourself.
options: 让搭档全程打断你、每犯一个错就立刻纠正
让搭档安静记录你出现了哪些失败模式，结束后对着五模式表逐条复盘
让搭档替你回答，你在旁边看他怎么做
两人各自练，练完只对比谁用的模型更新
options_en: Have the partner interrupt you throughout and correct each mistake the instant it happens.
Have the partner silently track which failure modes appear, then debrief against the five-mode table afterward.
Have the partner answer for you while you watch how they do it.
Practice separately and afterward only compare who used the newer model.
optionExplanations: 全程打断会毁掉表达连贯性，也练不出你在真实无干预下的自我纠偏。
对；安静观察+事后对表复盘，既保留真实答题状态，又拿到第三方视角标出的盲区。
看搭档答替代不了你自己练，抓不到你个人的走偏习惯。
比谁模型新完全跑题，练的是失败行为不是模型选型。
optionExplanations_en: Interrupting throughout destroys your flow and never trains the self-correction you'd need without intervention.
Correct — silent observation plus a table-based debrief keeps your answering authentic while giving an outside view of your blind spots.
Watching the partner answer can't replace your own reps and misses your personal drift habits.
Comparing whose model is newer misses the point; you're training failure behaviors, not model selection.
